sections.title: Diagonal Folding Concept
sections.content: When a square paper is folded along its diagonal, it forms a triangle. If folded again, the number of layers increases further. Diagonal folds change the orientation of shapes, so rotation must be considered while unfolding.

sections.title: Folding Circular Paper
sections.content: When a circular paper is folded into a semicircle and then into a quadrant, 2 folds create 4 layers. Any cut made in the folded part will repeat in all four sections when unfolded, forming a symmetrical circular pattern.

sections.title: Multiple and Asymmetric Cuts
sections.content: In Level 2, more than one cut may be made, such as a triangle cut at a corner and a circular hole near the center. Each cut repeats according to the number of layers. Total shapes formed = number of layers × number of distinct cuts (if applied to all layers).

sections.title: Shape and Orientation Tracking
sections.content: Options may describe both the number and direction of shapes. For example, triangles may point outward or inward depending on the fold. Diagonal folds often result in rotated shapes when opened.

sections.title: 4-Step Solution Method
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the type of fold (horizontal, vertical, diagonal, circular). Step 2: Count total layers formed. Step 3: Locate the exact position of each cut (center, edge, corner). Step 4: Apply symmetry and rotation to predict the final unfolded design.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Ignoring rotation caused by diagonal folds. 2. Forgetting to multiply cuts by total layers. 3. Misunderstanding inward and outward directions. 4. Choosing options without verifying symmetry.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 2 questions involve diagonal or circular folds and multiple cuts. Carefully track layers, apply symmetry, and consider rotation to determine both the exact count and correct orientation of shapes.

tricks.title: Diagonal Layer Rule
tricks.explanation: Each diagonal fold also doubles the layers like other folds.

tricks.title: Rotation Awareness Trick
tricks.explanation: Shapes formed after diagonal folds may appear rotated when unfolded.
tricks.example: A triangle cut may face different directions after opening.

tricks.title: Circular Quarter Logic
tricks.explanation: Two folds in a circle divide it into four equal sectors.
tricks.example: One hole in quadrant → 4 identical holes in full circle.

tricks.title: Multiple Cut Counting
tricks.explanation: Multiply each cut by the number of layers if it passes through all layers.

tricks.title: Center Shape Formation
tricks.explanation: Cuts near the folded center often form symmetrical central designs.
tricks.example: Small triangle near center → star-like pattern after unfolding.

tricks.title: Outward vs Inward Check
tricks.explanation: Check whether the base or vertex of shapes faces outward or toward the center.
tricks.example: Corner triangle cut → bases may face outward after unfolding.

tricks.title: Symmetry Elimination
tricks.explanation: Remove options that break symmetry across fold lines.
tricks.example: If design is symmetrical vertically and horizontally, asymmetrical options are incorrect.

tricks.title: 4-Step Mental Flow
tricks.explanation: Identify fold → Count layers → Locate cut → Apply symmetry and rotation.
tricks.example: 2 folds + 1 corner cut + 1 center hole → 4 corner shapes and 4 center holes.
